note: Draft register for Spec 047 (design D-09, PR #195 packet), opened 2026-10-21 under the runnable-experiments campaign plan approved by the owner as written the same date (D-09 = member 8; Asset B built inside this spec per E-6). Conventions as in Specs 032–042: requirement claims carry no falsification test where a gate or inspection is the operative check; boundaries carry the conditions under which each claim holds; evidence items carry observed_at from this draft because the cited facts were verified first-hand at drafting. The AEE lifecycle hooks have NOT run on this register; they are the freeze gate (tasks L4), and any recovery round they force changes claim text before any freeze digest is computed. ASM- ids name the assumptions each claim stands on: ASM-GAZETTEER-SPINE (the Spec 027 Stage 0 gazetteer, as pinned, is the site universe), ASM-PRIMARY-LAYER (the pinned Yajnadevam-compiled layer is the site-attributed corpus of record), ASM-PHASE104-RECORD (Phase-104's evaluation is the claim's record of standing), ASM-TWO-SOURCE-RULE (the design's two-source agreement rule is the classification's warrant), ASM-EXCAVATION-LITERATURE (published excavation/site literature states site functions admissibly), ASM-SHARES-CONTROL (comparing shares rather than counts is the design's size control), ASM-ROIF-SOURCE-POSTINGS (the 2025 Academia.edu postings are Roif's work of record, per the 2026-10-21 verification), ASM-COMPONENT-DECOMPOSITION (a bundled claim is adjudicated component by component), ASM-GATES-BEFORE-OUTCOME (integrity and classification gates precede any outcome quantity), ASM-APPEND-ONLY (outcomes append; frozen records are never edited), ASM-ROIF-GATE (campaign R-7 holds this member's results internal until the owner's publication act). FREEZE (2026-10-21): the AEE lifecycle hooks ran at the freeze act under aee 1.5.0; the full record is in aee/freeze-aee-note.md. Before the hooks ran, the freeze's own rulings were carried into the register (DD-047-13's all-UNMAPPED exception into the boundaries of F047-C13 and F047-C16; DD-047-10's seed, 20261021, into F047-C16's boundary). Round 0 (loadability): the register as drafted (0.5-draft) does not load under aee 1.5.0 - its evidence items carry free-form kind labels (program-record, design-source, campaign-record, verification-record) and source_quality labels (authoritative, program-record) that are not engine values, and the loader refuses them. Recovery to 0.6-draft normalised every evidence item to kind 'observed' and source_quality 'artifact' (the frozen-register form of Specs 036-039); refs, source_ids, directions, descriptions, and observed_at values are unchanged. Round 1 at after_specify over 0.6-draft returned iterate with 67 failure modes (18 irreducibility challenges; 27 shared-evidence independence-unmodelled records; 3 negation-conflict challenges - C06/C10, C07/C18, C10/C12; 19 FR-2.3 draft-cap records) and no claim below the 0.70 threshold (minimum propagated 0.72). Recovery to 0.7-draft: the 18 challenged claim texts were restated as single head propositions with their carried clauses moved into the boundaries verbatim-in-substance (propositions, falsifiers, and verdict rules unchanged; F047-C07's text was not challenged and stands as drafted); every multi-item claim's evidence gained mutual independent_of declarations naming the claim's other evidence source_ids (the within-claim pairs are distinct records - the Phase-104 evaluation, the design packet, the gazetteer, Spec 027's spec, the campaign plan, the Roif verification - and the declarations state that fact). Round 2 at after_specify over 0.7-draft returned 19 failure modes, all FR-2.3 draft-cap records; zero correctness failure modes; minimum propagated 0.72. after_plan and after_tasks over the same register: clean at first pass on the same terms (19 draft-cap records each). The gate reading is DD-047-16 (the DD-038-10 reading, adopted for this spec). This frozen register classifies no site, extracts no ledger-sign list, and counts nothing.

claims.text: An outcome under Spec 047 states only how inscriptions distribute across the frozen site-function classes of the Spec 027 gazetteer spine in the pinned primary corpus layer.
boundary: The scope is the distribution component of the claim, the 30-cluster gazetteer spine, its testable subset, and the primary layer. It excludes any statement about what any inscription records, about guilds, about Akkadian influence, about any other corpus or site set, and about Roif's thesis as a whole. Carried from the draft text: the outcome likewise states how Roif's named ledger-sign classes distribute across those classes; the two distribution objects are the claim's whole scope.
alternatives: the pooled claim-level verdict could be read as already covering the distribution question (it cannot: the claim stands UNTESTED for want of the classification this spec builds)
falsification_tests: the claim is falsified in scope if any Spec 047 output states a conclusion about a population, corpus, site set, or question outside the distribution component as bounded here

metadata.strongest_rival: the alternative reading in which a distribution verdict licenses a claim about the thesis as a whole
metadata.verdict_rule: scope is judged by inspection of every Spec 047 output against this boundary; any output exceeding it is a defect of the output, recorded as such, not a finding

claims.text: Within the test population of Spec 047, inscriptions concentrate at sites of the pooled ADMIN-TRADE-GATEWAY class.
boundary: The hypothesis is a statement about shares in the pinned primary layer over the frozen classification's testable sites, under the §6.3 criteria. It is not a statement about what inscriptions record, about sites outside the spine, or about the thesis's other two components. Carried from the draft text: the concentration claimed is the pooled class's share of inscriptions at least 1.5 times its share of testable sites, the label-shuffling test distinguishing the concentration from chance at the 5% level, with the ledger-sign classes named by Roif's text showing the same direction (the section 6.3 SUPPORTED clauses).

claims.text: Every Asset B classification uses exactly the six classes of spec §4.2 — gateway/border, administrative, port/trade, domestic, ritual, mixed/unknown — assigned by the mapping rule stated there from what a published source states about the site's primary function.
boundary: The vocabulary is closed, and the two derived groupings (pooled ADMIN-TRADE-GATEWAY; contrast domestic/ritual) are fixed in the same section. mixed/unknown belongs to neither grouping. No class may be added, split, or merged inside this campaign; a vocabulary defect is an amendment, not an edit.

claims.text: Test entry requires two independent published sources mapping a site to one identical section 4.2 class.
boundary: Each source is mapped on its own statement alone, with citation and locator recorded, before agreement is assessed. A reprint or a work repeating the same report's statement as its sole basis is not a second source. Agreement is identity of mapped classes, never closeness or worker judgement. Carried from the draft text: independence has the meaning spec section 4.3 gives it; each source states the site's function; the row is then AGREED, testable iff its class is not mixed/unknown.
falsification_tests: every AGREED row is re-checkable from the asset alone: two citations, two locators, two mapped classes, identical; a row failing that shape on inspection falsifies the build's compliance and the asset is unsound under spec §4.6

metadata.verdict_rule: AGREED status is judged mechanically from the recorded row shape; the §4.3 verification pass must pass for every AGREED row before the freeze (gate B3)

claims.text: Asset B freezes inside step 1 of Spec 047 under a SHA-256 digest of its committed file bytes.
boundary: The freeze point precedes the join of classes to counts, the ledger list's counting, and any consumer's test — D-10 (the D-10 specification) names the digest in its own inputs and re-asserts it at its step 0. Carried from the draft text: no mapping or status is derived from inscription content either, nor from sign distributions, nor from per-site inscription counts; the build is carried out without consulting the primary layer's per-site counts; the build record carries a dated attestation of both points naming the worker.

claims.text: A failed section 4.7 build gate leaves Asset B unfrozen.
boundary: A build failure is a statement about the build, not about Roif's claim, and the outcome record says so in the pre-written §7 wording. The number of testable sites is deliberately not a build gate: thinness is adjudicated by the test gate (F047-C15), where the design puts it. Carried from the draft text: the gates are coverage of exactly 30 rows (B1), citation completeness for every row's status (B2), the citation-verification pass for every AGREED row (B3), plus a truthful circularity attestation (B4); on a failure the spec closes at step 1 with design D-10 not-run by dependency closure.
alternatives: treating a low testable count as a build failure and rebuilding to a weaker standard inside the campaign (refused by the campaign plan: a failed asset is not rebuilt weaker inside the pass)
falsification_tests: each gate's check is recorded in the step-1 record before the freeze digest exists; a freeze digest present alongside a failed gate falsifies compliance

metadata.strongest_rival: gate-softening at build time, when the literature turns out messier than the draft hoped

boundary: The postings are the source of record because the held manuscript does not survive and the verification of 2026-10-21 establishes the identical-titled posting as publicly posted and citable. The program's model file and Phase-147 are not extraction sources. Extraction is blind to sign counts. Freeze ruling carried here (DD-047-13): if no entry maps, the list still freezes with its census, measure (b) does not run, and the execution proceeds on measure (a) alone under spec section 6.3's all-UNMAPPED partition. Carried from the draft text: extraction reads nothing else; a sign enters only if Roif's text explicitly assigns it an economic function (spec section 5); every entry carries its locator plus its crosswalk-mapped identifier; unmappable entries are recorded UNMAPPED, excluded by rule; the list freezes with Asset B under its own digest before any counting.
alternatives: extracting the list from the program's own summary of Roif (the model file), whose source metadata this draft found unreliable (spec §2.2)
falsification_tests: the extraction census is published with the outcome: entries sought, entered, and UNMAPPED, each entered entry re-checkable at its locator in the postings; an entry without a locator, or sourced elsewhere, falsifies compliance

boundary: These are spec §3's gates 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3; their failure class is INVALID. The census classes are joined, non-spine site (listed by name with counts), and no site value. No failure is repaired at run time; a repaired input is a new freeze, not a resumed run. Carried from the draft text: the gate failures are an input hash mismatch, a gazetteer spine failing to reproduce its recorded counts, plus a join census unable to account for every primary-layer record in exactly one of its three classes (spec section 3, gates 0.1 to 0.3; failure class INVALID).

claims.text: The distribution test does not run below twelve testable sites.
boundary: The 12-site floor is design D-09's, carried verbatim. The empty-side clause is this draft's completion of the same gate (DD-047-2): with one side empty the §6.2 ratio is undefined, so no quantity can honestly be computed. Asset B still freezes in this case; the floor is a test gate, not a build gate (F047-C12). Carried from the draft text: the test likewise does not run if either the pooled class or the contrast class is empty in the test population (DD-047-2); the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE with the classification itself as the finding, its disagreements published in full, with no distribution quantity computed.
alternatives: computing the shares anyway on a thin classification because the numbers would be interesting (refused: the design makes the classification the finding in exactly this case)

evidence.description: Design D-09 (PR #195 packet, §D-09, read in full at this draft): the question, hypothesis, falsifier, step-1 classification build under the two-source agreement rule, step-2 measures, and criteria this spec registers.

claims.text: The verdict follows the section 6.3 partition mechanically.
boundary: No threshold, margin, shuffle count, or clause is adjusted for the observed data. The permutation seed is fixed at this spec's freeze and recorded in the freeze record, before any count exists. The partition is exhaustive: every (R, p, R_ledger) triple lands in exactly one outcome. Freeze rulings carried here: the seed is 20261021 (DD-047-10); and in the all-UNMAPPED case of spec section 5 (no ledger entry maps, DD-047-13) R_ledger is not computed and the partition runs on (R, p) alone exactly as spec section 6.3's all-UNMAPPED paragraph states, with the vacated ledger clause stated openly in the outcome record. Carried from the draft text: SUPPORTED iff the ratio is at least 1.5 with the permutation test (9,999 label shuffles) rejecting at the 5% level plus the ledger-sign ratio above 1.0; NOT SUPPORTED iff the ratio is at or below 1.0 or the permutation test does not reject; INCONCLUSIVE in every remaining case.
alternatives: re-deriving thresholds from the test population once its size is known (refused: the design fixes the 1.5 ratio, the 5% level, and the 9,999 shuffles in advance)
falsification_tests: the verdict assignment is mechanical from the recorded quantities; any verdict not following this rule from its run's numbers falsifies the outcome record, and any reader can recompute it

metadata.strongest_rival: post-hoc rule-shopping once the ratios are known — in particular, softening a permutation failure into INCONCLUSIVE contrary to the design's NOT SUPPORTED clause
metadata.verdict_rule: verdicts are recomputed from the published quantities by any reader; the rule text here and in spec §6.3 is frozen before execution

evidence.description: Design D-09 (PR #195 packet, §D-09, read in full at this draft): the question, hypothesis, falsifier, step-1 classification build under the two-source agreement rule, step-2 measures, and criteria this spec registers.

claims.text: The section 6.4 sensitivities are reported beside the primary in every outcome product.
boundary: Sensitivities expose classification contestability and excavation bias; they are not alternate verdicts. A sensitivity that flatly contradicts the primary is reported as such, prominently — what it may not do is replace the headline word, which only the §6.3 partition assigns. Carried from the draft text: the sensitivities are the each-source-alone recomputations plus the five-largest-sites recomputation; no sensitivity result changes the headline verdict.
alternatives: promoting the source-alone run that agrees with the hypothesis to co-primary status after the fact (refused: primacy is fixed here, before execution)
falsification_tests: an outcome product lacking either sensitivity, or carrying a headline word traceable to a sensitivity rather than to the §6.3 partition, falsifies compliance

metadata.strongest_rival: sensitivity-shopping: quoting whichever recomputation flatters the claim and burying the other in an appendix
metadata.verdict_rule: the §9 reporting obligations make both sensitivities headline-paragraph-adjacent deliverables; their absence is a defect of the product, recorded as such

claims.text: Every record of Spec 047 stays internal under the Roif gate.
boundary: The 2026-10-21 verification — Roif's work publicly posted and citable — satisfies the gate's evidence condition but clears nothing by itself: under campaign E-2/R-7 the owner's publication act is separate and later, for this member exactly as for D-02, D-04, and D-10. Internal records, internal status reporting in the prescribed form, and the verdict records themselves are not publication.
